data.review_body:
Temu is just every other poor app, it's basically the same as Wish.com but with basically just a gambling aesthetic. Do not use this website or app, it's bait and switch, sure you get free stuff- but it's not really free stuff. You have to pay money on other items indirectly to "lower" the money left required to get your 0.01 cent phone! Yet, let's say you do fill out all the goals. Your order will more than likely be canceled stating "security issues" even though it's all throughout the app systems that even led you to get there. But, here is the trick. The other items you paid for to get your 1 cent item aren't cancelled, and if you contact support. They are useless and tell you what you already know, and if you ask for something other than "security issues", it's just stated again, just in different wording. 

I'll say it once again, do not buy from Temu. 

As for Temu's parent company, PDD Holdings, which has a long history of intense controversy, legal battles, and regulatory scrutiny regarding data security and corporate fraud. Cybersecurity experts, international regulators, and investor groups have repeatedly flagged the company for deceptive and suspicious practices. Take your business someplace else.
data.review_headline: Temu is just every other poor app, just with gambling added into it.

data.review_body:
All I can say is that the clothing items I ordered must be very photographic.
They looked nothing like what I ordered.
Cheap and under sized.
First and last order.
I’m getting bombarded with emails from Temu, offering me 4 free gifts plus more recently my money back as a reward.
No thanks.
I haven’t contacted Temu regarding my goods.
Once bitten, twice shy.
I will donate the clothing to a charity shop.
Items shipped from China, and took an inordinate time to arrive.

Edit. Temu want to identify myself by quoting order number and name & address.
If I don’t do this Trustpilot treats it as a fake review.
I know that my review disappears at the slightest excuse.
Details given as requested.
data.review_headline: You get what you pay for. Disappointing.

Very misleading promotions and a deliberately confusing shopping experience. I placed an order because Temu clearly showed I had claimed 6 free gifts, but later 4 of them were removed without any explanation.

The shopping screen feels intentionally cluttered to distract customers from what's actually being added or removed from their order. You might fool people once, but once they realize what's happening, you lose their trust. I won't be ordering from Temu again.
